explicit_source: Let H=[|00>]+[|01>+|10>]+[|03>+|12>]+[|02>+|11>]+[sqrt(2)|13>+|10>] on 2x4, and Q=[|10>+|02>]+[|20>+|12>]+[|00>+|21>]+[|01>+|22>] on 3x3. Regroup H tensor Q across Alice=(A_H,A_Q), Bob=(B_H,B_Q), retain Alice basis (0,0),(0,1),(0,2),(1,1), and index Bob as 3*b_H+b_Q. Call the resulting unnormalized 4x12 operator R; tr R=44. This explicit additive definition is the sole source used in our 495-cut certificates. Exact Q(sqrt2) arithmetic gives H>=0, H^Gamma>=0, both ranks5, and verifies Q^Gamma as four projectors; thus R is PPT.
horodecki_entanglement: The range of H consists of 2x4 matrices [[a,b,d,c],[b+e,d,c,sqrt(2)*e]]. The kernel of H^Gamma is spanned by -|00>+|11>, -|01>+|12>, and -|02>-(1/sqrt(2))|10>+|13>; exact arithmetic verifies all three and rank5. Consider a product vector in ran H whose Bob-partial conjugate lies in ran H^Gamma. If its first Alice row is zero it is a multiple of |1> tensor (|0>+sqrt(2)|3>). Otherwise write the second row as t times the first. For t=0 the vector is a multiple of |00>, whose partial conjugate fails the first kernel condition. For t!=0 its b coefficient is nonzero; normalize b=1. The product equations give d=t, c=t^2, e=t^3/sqrt(2), a=t^-1+t^2/sqrt(2), so the vector is (|0>+t|1>) tensor (a|0>+|1>+t|2>+t^2|3>). Partial conjugation of the Bob factor and orthogonality to the first two kernel vectors require conjugate(a)=t and |t|^2=1. Orthogonality to the third gives -conjugate(t)-(t*conjugate(a))/sqrt(2)+t*conjugate(t)^2=0, which reduces to -t^2/sqrt(2)=0, a contradiction. Hence every compatible product vector lies in the single product line above, while rank H=5. If H were separable, its product summands and their partial conjugates would have to lie in both respective ranges; one line cannot span rank5. Thus H is entangled PPT and, as a 2x4 state, has SN exactly2.
independent_4x12_sn3_proof: In our Alice row ordering 0,1,2,3 and Bob 0..11, let the core use Alice rows1,3 and Bob columns J=(0,3,6,9). Direct exact contraction gives core(R)=H. Every vector X in ran R satisfies: rows1 and3 vanish at columns J+1=(1,4,7,10); row2 at J+1 equals row0 at J; and row1 at J equals row0 at J+2=(2,5,8,11). These linear identities are checked on all20 source kets and hence hold on the entire range. Suppose rank(X)<=2 but its core rows1,3 have rank2. They then span all rows of X. Their zeros at J+1 force row2 at J+1=0, hence row0 at J=0. Independence of the two core rows implies row0 is the zero linear combination and therefore vanishes everywhere. The final range identity then forces row1 at J=0, contradicting rank2 of the core. Thus the core of every SR<=2 range vector has rank<=1. If R were SN<=2, projecting such a decomposition to the core would decompose H into product projectors, contradicting its proven entanglement. Hence SN(R)>=3. Every one of the 20 defining tensor kets after the Alice projection occupies at most three Alice rows, so SN(R)<=3. Thus SN(R)=3 exactly.
